subject: SignalPath security intake — questionnaire choice & data residency questions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma@signalpath.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + questionnaire preference (SIG / CAIQ / custom)

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have a clear intake path on the security side:

- What we heard: SignalPath wants predictable latency for inference, private tenancy options, and clarity on data residency + PHI handling.
- Security intake options: we can start with a CAIQ prefill (fastest), a full SIG (more comprehensive), or a custom questionnaire focused on HIPAA/GDPR items.

A few clarifying questions to help us pick the right path:
1) Do you consider any of your traffic PHI (protected health information) under HIPAA? If yes, we will need to discuss a BAA.
2) Are you able to share a recent SOC 2 Type II report or will you need us to accept SOC 2 through a portal/attestation?
3) Data residency: which regions/countries must data remain in? (US-only, EU, APAC subsets?)
4) SSO / IdP: do you support SAML/Okta? If so, please confirm whether you can exchange metadata or would prefer a temporary service account.

I've attached the CAIQ template we typically prefill to speed things up. If you prefer SIG, we can route that for a deeper evidence collection (longer lead time). Let me know which you prefer and any timeline constraints for your procurement review.

Next step: once you confirm, Soojin will own the CAIQ prefill and Karthik will coordinate SOC 2/BAA items.

Thanks —
Marcus
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: CAIQ_template.xlsx]
From: Emma Rodriguez <emma@signalpath.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: SignalPath Security <security@signalpath.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + questionnaire preference (SIG / CAIQ / custom)

Marcus — thanks for the summary and for the template. Short answers below: 

- PHI: yes, SignalPath processes limited PHI for a subset of our healthcare customers (pseudonymized internally but still within HIPAA scope). We will need a BAA.
- SOC 2: we completed a SOC 2 Type II in March 2027. We can share the report under NDA or grant portal access — whichever works better for you.
- Data residency: primary requirement is US for PHI; non-PHI data can be replicated to EU for our EU customers but it's not required for all workloads.
- SSO/IdP: we use Okta and can exchange IdP metadata.

Preference: we'd like Redwood to start with a CAIQ prefill so we can iterate quickly, then expand to SIG for any deeper evidence requests. Timeline: procurement would like initial answers by end of next week (May 21).

I'll attach a short system overview that might help the prefill. Also: one quick question — for encryption-at-rest key management, do you support customer-managed keys (KMIP/HSM) or only provider-managed keys?

Emma
Head of Security Ops
SignalPath
[Attachment: SignalPath-System-Overview.pdf]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SignalPath preference + PHI note — action items

Karthik / Soojin — forwarding Emma's reply. TL;DR: they process PHI and require a BAA; SOC 2 Type II available (March 2027); prefer CAIQ then SIG; timeline ~ May 21 for initial answers.

Please action: 
- Soojin: start prefill on the CAIQ_template.xlsx. Focus first on the dataflow, PHI handling, and access controls sections. Use the attached SignalPath-System-Overview as source. Please flag anything that needs engineering input.
- Karthik: I'll need you to review SOC 2 props and BAA language. If they require a BAA we'll escalate legal — but confirm whether current infra + private deploy options meet their PHI requirements.

Also capture an answer re: CMK (customer-managed keys) — our hosted product currently supports provider-managed keys; Dedicated/Private can support customer-managed KMS integrations. I'll draft a short explainer for procurement.

I'll set a hard internal deliverable to have the CAIQ draft to share with Emma by 2027-05-18 so they can review ahead of their procurement deadline.

Thanks — Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SignalPath preference + PHI note — action items

Ack — I'll pull the SOC 2 report and confirm the scope items (in-scope services, vendor subservice orgs, encryption controls) and start a short draft of BAA points to share with Legal.

Sooj: if you run into anything that needs a deeper runbook or evidence (e.g., network ACL exports, firewall configs), call it out and I'll route to infra.

Karthik
From: Emma Rodriguez <emma@signalpath.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: SignalPath Security <security@signalpath.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + questionnaire preference (SIG / CAIQ / custom)

Thanks Marcus — that plan works. We'll expect the CAIQ draft by 5/18. Once we see that, our security ops will flag any SIG-level follow-ups.

Regarding keys: for most customers we accept provider-managed keys; a small number require CMKs (HSM/KMS). If Redwood supports CMK for Private deployment, please include the configuration steps in your reply so we can show it to procurement.

We'll upload supporting docs (SOC 2 copy and a vendor system diagram) to the Drive link you provided. If you need portal access instead, tell me and we'll grant it.

Best,
Emma

--- Thread notes (internal) ---
Created deliverables: CAIQ draft (owner: soojin_lee) due 2027-05-18; SOC2 review & BAA draft (owner: karthik_iyer) due 2027-05-17.
Evidence expected from SignalPath: SOC2 Type II report (March 2027), system diagram, and any requested firewall/network artifacts.
Suggested next internal meeting: quick 20-min sync 2027-05-15 10:00 PT to triage evidence asks.
